paragraphs: Decision center: the work of Electrical and Electronic Equipment Assemblers is to turn these front-end conditions — drawings and processes and work instructions and work orders, materials and components and wire harnesses and fixtures and test equipment, the safety conditions for anti-static protection and protective equipment and electrical work and chemicals and noise, and the requirements for cycle time and quality and traceability and delivery — into executable, reviewable and accountable assembly and self-inspection results: first confirm the assembly and self-inspection requirements by drawings and processes and work orders and verify materials and components and fixtures, then complete soldering and crimping and winding and fastening and wiring and dispensing and cleaning according to the specifications, then measure and visually inspect and functionally test according to standards and record data and mark status, and during that period work according to anti-static and protective equipment and electrical and chemical and noise requirements and maintain 5S and equipment checks, then rework or quarantine nonconforming items and honestly report abnormalities, and finally fill in assembly and inspection and traceability records and complete handover. The focus of judgment is not "whether one assembles fast", but whether, along the chain of "preparation and verification—assembly and self-inspection—records and traceability and abnormalities", one can hold four things — process accuracy, dimensional and electrical conformity, protective and anti-static compliance and data traceability — and leave a checkable record at every step.

Worth trying first: being willing to be responsible for assembly quality and safety and traceability and to accept questioning from the supervisor and quality control and the crew; being able to switch pace among production line cycle time and multiple stations and changeovers; being willing to act according to drawings and processes and anti-static and safety requirements and to honestly report abnormalities; and being able to accept repeated work and long periods of standing and eye and hand use driven by shifts and overtime and cycle time and appraisal cycles.

Think carefully: if you expect this job to be just casual assembling, or to be only about speed with no concern for drawings and quality, or you are unwilling to act according to drawings and processes and anti-static and safety requirements, or you avoid responsibility for quality and traceability and safety, or you treat one experience as a conclusion and skip self-inspection and records on that basis, or you find it hard to keep patience and accuracy under cycle time and repetition and overtime and multiple shifts, then the actual experience usually does not match the expectation.

Low-risk check: using the fictional drawings and processes and bill of materials provided on this page, complete a paper exercise of "writing the material verification, assembly steps, self-inspection, records and protection check for an assembly process", verifying only whether you are willing to check items one by one against drawings and processes and data and to honestly mark uncertainty. The exercise uses fictional materials, does not constitute a quality release or safety or legal conclusion, and is not equivalent to an occupational skill grade certificate or a work qualification.

Decision center: whether drawings and processes and work orders and materials and cycle time conditions can be turned into assembly and self-inspection results that the supervisor and quality control and the crew and the next process can all take up and review.

The work rhythm is jointly determined by shifts and cycle time and overtime and changeovers and delivery and appraisal points; repeated work and long periods of standing and eye and hand use are common, and cycle time and time pressure must be handled while protecting safety and quality.

Similar names do not mean the same duties: this page is O*NET-SOC 51-2022.00 Electrical and Electronic Equipment Assemblers. Adjacent roles — electromechanical equipment assemblers (51-2023), coil winders, tapers, and finishers (51-2021), team assemblers (51-2092 / 51-2099), electrical and electronic equipment installers and repairers (49-2094), machinists (51-4041), computer numerically controlled tool operators (51-9161), quality control inspectors (51-9061), first-line supervisors of production and operating workers (51-1011), welders, cutters, solderers, and brazers (51-4121), engine and other machine assemblers (51-2031), and timing device assemblers and adjusters (51-2061) — have different objects and authorizations; this occupation is also not equivalent to a quality release or process design post. Quality release and process and safety and inspection requirements follow the laws and regulations of the relevant jurisdiction and unit rules, are not inferred from job titles, and no one may issue quality and safety or legal conclusions externally beyond authorization.

You can use AI as a controlled aid for process and material and record support, but you cannot treat generated content as unreviewed assembly parameters or inspection criteria or quality and safety conclusions; assembly and self-inspection and release and safety remain the responsibility of certified and named responsible persons and units.

The fit judgment should be made by combining whether you can take responsibility for assembly quality and safety and traceability, whether you can act according to drawings and processes and anti-static requirements and data, whether you can communicate under cycle time and repetition and overtime and escalate according to the rules, and whether you are clear about the boundaries of your authority over process and inspection and release and traceability; it is not replaced by a self-assessment of "being fast" or "being patient"; all of this must be confirmed in supervised assembly internships and supervisor mentoring.

All exercises on this page use fictional materials; real process and inspection and release and safety decisions must be undertaken by personnel who hold the appropriate qualifications and act in accordance with the laws and regulations of the relevant jurisdiction and the requirements of competent authorities and unit rules; individuals may not issue quality and safety or legal conclusions externally beyond their authorization, and this page does not constitute any quality or safety or legal advice.

The work object of this occupation is electrical and electronic equipment and components, with interface to multiple parties: drawings and processes and work instructions and work orders, materials and components and wire harnesses and connectors and fixtures and test equipment, the safety conditions for anti-static protection and protective equipment and electrical work and chemicals and noise, cycle time and changeover and delivery and traceability requirements, and self-inspection and rework and abnormality reporting arrangements. The output is assembly results that meet drawings and processes and quality requirements: soldering and crimping and winding and fastening and wiring and dispensing and cleaning completed according to process and cycle time, measurement and visual inspection and functional testing completed according to standards, assembly and inspection and traceability and abnormality records completed according to the rules, and conforming deliverable items or items and status quarantined and reworked according to the process. The basis for judgment is drawings and processes and data and unit rules, not personal experience or job title.

Judgment one: whether drawings and processes and work orders and materials align — whether components and wire harnesses and polarity and models are verified against drawings and processes and work orders and the bill of materials, rather than taking materials by impression.

Judgment two: whether assembly actions follow the specifications — whether soldering temperature and time and crimping force and winding turns and fastening torque and dispensing amount are completed according to process, rather than operated at will.

Judgment three: whether self-inspection and measurement and functional testing follow standards — whether measurement and visual inspection and functional testing are done according to inspection criteria and data are recorded and status marked, rather than released by feeling.

Judgment four: whether anti-static and protection and electrical and chemical requirements are upheld — whether work is done according to anti-static and protective equipment and electrical and chemical and noise and ventilation requirements and good 5S and equipment checks are maintained, rather than skipping steps.

Judgment five: whether abnormalities and rework and quarantine follow the process — whether nonconforming items are quarantined according to the rules and honestly reported and reworked or scrapped, rather than handled on one's own or concealed.

Judgment six: whether the boundaries of data and traceability and delivery and external conclusions are upheld — whether assembly and inspection and batch and traceability records are filled in according to the rules, without issuing quality and safety or legal conclusions externally beyond authorization, and seeking instructions and reporting according to the rules when something is abnormal.

Environment and rhythm: mainly workshops and production lines and workstations, with interaction with the supervisor and quality control and the crew; the rhythm is driven by shifts and cycle time and overtime and changeovers and delivery points, and repeated work and long periods of standing and eye and hand use are common; specific arrangements and hours follow the unit and jurisdiction.

The work of Electrical and Electronic Equipment Assemblers can be divided into three connected but independent work areas. The first category is preparation and verification: take tasks according to work orders and drawings and processes and work instructions and verify the version, collect and verify materials and components and wire harnesses and connectors and fixtures and test equipment and confirm models and polarity and quantities, and check anti-static and protective equipment and electrical and fixture status and prepare record forms. The second category is assembly and self-inspection: complete soldering and crimping and winding and fastening and wiring and dispensing and cleaning and assembly according to process and cycle time, measure and visually inspect and functionally test according to standards and record data and mark status, and maintain workstation 5S and material identification and error proofing. The third category is records and abnormalities and delivery: fill in assembly and inspection and batch and traceability records, quarantine and rework or scrap nonconforming items according to the process and honestly report abnormalities and line stop requests, cooperate with quality control and process and equipment staff on handling and take part in improvement, and finally complete handover. All three work areas proceed within drawings, processes, quality, data and safety requirements.

Core purpose

To turn drawings and processes and work orders and materials and cycle time conditions into executable and reviewable and accountable assembly and self-inspection results: clear materials and version, assembly according to specifications, evidence-based self-inspection and records, and protection and abnormalities that hold their boundaries.

In this work, which judgments are most prone to error, and how should they be checked?

Common errors cluster in four categories: first, material and version and polarity verification is inadequate, leading to wrong assembly and whole-batch rework and customer complaints; second, assembly is judged by experience rather than process and measurement, leading to nonconforming dimensions and electrical performance and appearance; third, anti-static and protection and electrical and chemical and noise requirements are not handled according to the rules, leading to electrostatic damage and work injuries and occupational disease risks; fourth, self-inspection and records and traceability and abnormalities do not follow the process, leading to nonconforming items flowing to the next process and responsibility that cannot be traced. The way to check is that each item has a reviewable basis: task and version and material verification records, process and assembly and parameter records, measurement and visual inspection and functional testing and status marking records, anti-static and protection and fixture check records, and abnormality and rework and traceability records — not memory or verbal agreement.

When comparing, three things govern: first, the work object (electromechanical equipment and assemblies, coil windings, team assembly tasks, electrical and electronic equipment, products and processes, crew production); second, the basis and authorization (drawings and processes and quality and data and unit rules, assembly drawings and processes, winding and finishing processes, crew work instructions, equipment manuals and codes, inspection standards and sampling plans, and production plans and crew rules, each as applicable); third, outputs and responsibility (who is responsible for electrical and electronic equipment assembly and self-inspection, who for electromechanical equipment and assemblies, who for coil windings, who for team assembly, who for electrical and electronic equipment installation and repair, who for product and process inspection judgments, and who for crew production). Where the three conflict, the actual duties of the post and the laws and regulations and institutional rules govern.

The basis for choice can follow three threads: if you want to take on the assembly and self-inspection and traceability of electrical and electronic equipment and components, this page's occupation is the closest; if you want to work in electromechanical equipment and assembly assembly, coil winding and finishing, team assembly, electrical and electronic equipment installation and repair, product and process inspection, or crew production management, then electromechanical equipment assemblers, coil winders tapers and finishers, team assemblers, electrical and electronic equipment installers and repairers, quality control inspectors, and first-line supervisors of production and operating workers are adjacent paths. paragraphs: Electromechanical equipment assemblers (51-2023.00)

Assemble electromechanical equipment and assemblies and motion and transmission parts according to assembly drawings and processes and commission and self-inspect them, usually involving the coordination of mechanical and electrical and pneumatic work.

Objects and technology differ: electromechanical equipment assemblers focus on electromechanical equipment and assemblies, involving mechanical and electrical and pneumatic coordination and commissioning; this page's occupation focuses on electrical and electronic equipment and components, mainly soldering and crimping and winding and wiring and dispensing and functional testing. The objects and technology differ and cannot be interchanged by equipment name.

If you want to work in electromechanical equipment and assembly assembly and commissioning, the electromechanical equipment assembler direction is an option; if you want to bear assembly and self-inspection responsibility for electrical and electronic equipment and components, this page's occupation is closer.
Coil winders, tapers, and finishers (51-2021.00)
Wind coils and windings according to winding and finishing processes and finish and varnish impregnate and test them, usually for motors and transformers and inductive components.

Processes and objects differ: coil winders, tapers, and finishers specialize in coil winding and finishing and varnish impregnation, with a relatively specialized process; this page's occupation covers complete unit and component level assembly and self-inspection and traceability, involving multiple processes and coordination with the previous and next processes. The processes and objects differ and cannot substitute for each other.

If you want to specialize in winding and finishing processes, the coil winder, taper, and finisher direction is an option; if you want to bear component and complete unit assembly and self-inspection and traceability responsibility, this page's occupation is more suitable.
Team assemblers (51-2092.00)

Duties and organization differ: team assemblers complete assembly and manufacturing tasks through small-group collaboration and division of labor according to crew work instructions, with work organization and rhythm based on teams and multi-skilled workers; this page's occupation is based on workstations and cycle time and process and self-inspection and records, so the work organization and authorization differ and cannot be interchanged by crew name.

If you want to complete assembly tasks through small-group collaboration, the team assembler direction is an option; if you want to bear assembly and self-inspection and traceability responsibility by workstation and process, this page's occupation is closer.
Electrical and electronic equipment installers and repairers (49-2094.00)

Duties and authorization differ: electrical and electronic equipment installers and repairers are responsible for the installation and commissioning and repair of electrical and electronic equipment, mainly on-site and equipment operation and repair; this page's occupation is responsible for the assembly and self-inspection of electrical and electronic equipment and components and usually does not bear on-site installation and repair and equipment release duties, so the duties and authorization differ and cannot substitute for each other.

If you want to work in electrical and electronic equipment installation and repair, that direction is an option; if you want to bear assembly and self-inspection and traceability responsibility, this page's occupation is more suitable.
Quality control inspectors (51-9061.00)

Duties and authorization differ: quality control inspectors measure and judge and record products and processes according to inspection standards and sampling plans and issue inspection conclusions; this page's occupation covers process and assembly and self-inspection and records and usually does not bear independent inspection judgment and quality release duties, so the authorization differs and cannot substitute for each other.

If you want to work in product and process inspection and judgment, the quality control inspector direction is an option; if you want to bear assembly and self-inspection and traceability responsibility, this page's occupation is closer.
First-line supervisors of production and operating workers (51-1011.00)

Duties and authorization differ: first-line supervisors of production and operating workers are responsible for crew scheduling and dispatching and tracking and appraisal and on-site management, based on production plans and crew rules; this page's occupation bears specific assembly and self-inspection and recording duties, so the levels of duty and authorization differ and cannot substitute for each other.

If you want to take on crew production management responsibility, the first-line supervisor direction is an option; if you want to focus on assembly and self-inspection and traceability, this page's occupation is more suitable.

description.text: Electrical and Electronic Equipment Assemblers (O*NET-SOC 51-2022.00) assemble electrical and electronic equipment and components according to drawings and processes and self-inspect: verifying work orders and materials and version and polarity, completing soldering and crimping and winding and fastening and wiring and dispensing and cleaning according to process and cycle time, measuring and visually inspecting and functionally testing according to standards and recording data and marking status, working according to anti-static and protection and safety requirements and maintaining 5S, and filling in batch and traceability records and quarantining and reworking and reporting nonconforming items. United States basis: BLS 2025 wage data median 45,850 USD per year (22.04 USD per hour, median only); 2024 employment about 261,400, 2024—2034 projection "faster than average (5% to 6%)" with about 29,600 projected openings; preparation level Job Zone 1-2, interest code RCI. Mainland China: safety training and labor protection and occupational health and skill grades are carried out in accordance with the Work Safety Law and the Law on the Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases and national occupational skill standards; public statistics have not established an occupation-level wage basis, and this page visibly marks the gap in the relevant places.

subject.name: Electrical and Electronic Equipment Assemblers
subject.summary: Electrical and Electronic Equipment Assemblers (United States side O*NET-SOC 51-2022.00, Electrical and Electronic Equipment Assemblers) is an assembly post for electrical and electronic equipment and components: assembling electrical and electronic equipment and components according to drawings and processes and work instructions and completing assembly and self-inspection on a production line or at a workstation to cycle time; the work includes taking tasks by work orders and drawings and processes and verifying the version, collecting and verifying materials and components and wire harnesses and connectors and fixtures and test equipment, checking anti-static and protective equipment and electrical and fixture status, completing soldering and crimping and winding and fastening and wiring and dispensing and cleaning according to process and cycle time, measuring and visually inspecting and functionally testing according to standards and recording data and marking status, maintaining workstation 5S and material identification and error proofing, filling in assembly and inspection and batch and traceability records, quarantining and reworking or scrapping nonconforming items according to the process and honestly reporting abnormalities and line stop requests, cooperating with quality control and process and equipment staff on handling and taking part in improvement, and completing handover. United States basis: BLS 2025 wage data median 45,850 USD per year (22.04 USD per hour; that source provides only the median and does not provide the 10/25/75/90 percentiles); the O*NET summary page gives 2024 employment of about 261,400, a 2024—2034 projection of "faster than average (Faster than average, 5% to 6%)" and about 29,600 projected openings for 2024—2034 (total for the projection period); the preparation level is Job Zone 1-2 (SVP below 6.0), education feedback is 46% high school or equivalent and 35% below high school, the interest code is RCI, and there are 17 tasks. Mainland China basis: employee safety training and labor protection and protection against harmful work are carried out in accordance with the Work Safety Law of the People's Republic of China and the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases and unit safety and quality rules; occupational skills can be assessed for skill grades according to national occupational skill standards (electronic equipment installer and electronic device assembler, etc.). Public statistics have not established an occupation-level wage basis corresponding to this occupation, and this page preserves the gap faithfully, with the industry average wage serving only as a visible industry proxy.
